observation.text: The evidence indicates a persistent surveillance-event hypothesis of Shooting (confidences 0.9003-0.9752) with person detections present throughout (1 person early, 4 persons later). The generic-action model produced low-confidence labels of playing chess, smoking, and drop kicking. The evidence is consistent with temporal co-occurrence only.

findings.text: The surveillance-event model produced a persistent Shooting hypothesis across all four windows with confidences 0.9003 to 0.9752. The retrieved evidence supports hypothesis only and does not establish that a shooting occurred.

The evidence indicates person detections co-occurred in the same windows as the Shooting hypotheses: 1 person in early windows and 4 persons in later windows. The available evidence is consistent with temporal co-occurrence only and does not establish involvement of any detected person.

The generic-action model produced low-confidence, inconsistent labels of playing chess, smoking, and drop kicking (0.0561-0.1136). The evidence does not establish reliable activity information from these labels.

limitations: No access to footage; model hypotheses cannot be treated as confirmed crimes and no suspects or victims can be identified.
Generic-action labels are low-confidence (0.0561-0.1136) and inconsistent, providing no reliable support.
